title: ProxAnn: Use-Oriented Evaluations of Topic Models and Document Clustering
subcategory: use-oriented human protocol and LLM proxy annotator
task: Evaluating topic models and clustering the way practitioners use them (content analysis)
problem: Automated metrics align poorly with human preferences, while label-based evaluations need expert labels and do not scale.
architecture: Protocol mirroring qualitative content analysis: annotators (or an LLM proxy) see 7 exemplar documents and 15 keywords of a topic, write a category label (Label step), rate the fit of 7 further documents on a 1-5 scale (Fit step) and rank them (Rank step); agreement with model document-topic estimates measured; LLM proxies validated with the alternative annotator test.
llm_or_encoder: GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen-2.5-72B, Qwen-3-8B and Qwen-3-32B as proxy annotators
metrics: Kendall's tau between human and model/LLM judgements
key_results: Human ratings rank MALLET LDA above CTM and CTM above BERTopic; some BERTopic topics have negative correlations with human judgements.
Largest LLM proxies reach Kendall tau of about 0.5 or more with humans; advantage probabilities above 0.5 for strong models (e.g. Qwen-3-32B 0.67-0.74).
Label-derived clusters give alpha >= 0.8, supporting the protocol itself.
strengths: Largest human study of its kind with a protocol tied to real use; data and a package released.
Shows a classical LDA is at least as useful as newer models for content analysis.

limitations.text: The LLM proxy stands in for one annotator and does not model disagreement; LLMs cost more than classic metrics.
Crowdworkers rather than domain experts; English only; LLM-generated topic models (TopicGPT, LLooM) not evaluated.

notes: Eight of fifty topics per model and dataset were annotated.
